articles.title: Judge rules the Pentagon’s supply chain risk label for Anthropic unlawful
articles.description: A federal judge ruled the Pentagon’s decision to label AI company Anthropic a ‘supply chain risk’ violated the law and ordered the designation be removed Thursday evening.

articles.title: The global AI race has entered a new phase, and China has the cost advantage: Brookings Institution
articles.description: Brookings Institution’s Kyle Chan says Chinese AI models could gain ground by offering greater value at lower cost, even if they lag US rivals at the frontier. He also explains how China’s AI companies are finding new ways to monetize open-source models.

articles.title: Strength in Korean stocks and memory chipmakers to continue, says David Riedel
articles.description: David Riedel of Riedel Research Group remains bullish on Korean memory chipmakers, which he describes as “the holders of the keys” to continued AI growth. He also explains why Korean high-voltage equipment manufacturers are his highest-conviction investment call.

articles.title: BOJ to hike in September as worries mount over inflation: Economist
articles.description: Kazuo Momma from Mizuho Research Institute says he expects the BOJ to hike in September on the back of hotter-than-expected Tokyo CPI data. He also shares that if the BOJ does not hike, the yen will likely continue its weakening slide.

articles.title: AI Circular financing is not a red flag: Aptus Capital Advisors
articles.description: David Wagner of Aptus Capital Advisors says the data center trade may face sentiment-driven pressure in H2 2026, rather than fundamental weakness. He sees Nvidia share price reaching $275 in the coming months and notes circular financing not is not a red flag, but is a sign that the AI and compute industry is maturing.

articles.title: The US switch in shingles vaccines revealed an unexpected heart health pattern
articles.description: In a natural experiment involving 72,920 propensity-matched US adults aged 60 years and older, recombinant shingles vaccination was associated with a 9% lower cardiovascular disease burden over seven years compared with the live attenuated vaccine. Lower burdens of ischemic heart disease and heart failure were seen in both sexes, while ischemic stroke was significantly lower only among men, supporting further clinical trials and mechanistic studies

articles.title: Birth-related PTSD may go undiagnosed among thousands of new mothers
articles.description: Tens of thousands of new mums across Britain may be suffering undiagnosed PTSD following childbirth, according to a University of East Anglia report.

articles.title: Parkinson’s disease imposes €22.8 billion economic burden across Europe
articles.description: The annual societal cost of Parkinson's disease across Europe reached €22.8 billion in 2019, equivalent to €28.8 billion at 2025 prices, a new study published today in Movement Disorders has shown.

articles.title: Americans differ widely in understanding of plant-based diets
articles.description: When referring to diet, the term "plant-based" has mixed interpretations among U.S. adults, and its meaning varies significantly among demographic groups, according to new research published in the American Journal of Lifestyle Medicine.

articles.title: Brain shrinkage biomarker may predict early-onset Alzheimer’s progression
articles.description: In people diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer's disease, a biomarker tool that detects shrinkage of the brain's gray matter may predict how quickly someone may progress from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to dementia, according to a new study published August 26, 2026, in Neurology, an official journal of the American Academy of Neurology.

articles.title: Internet-controlled brain implant enables remote neural stimulation and drug delivery
articles.description: A researcher in Chicago remotely controls a miniaturized brain implant in Daejeon, Korea - over the internet. Korean researchers have developed a wireless device that can deliver drugs and light to precisely modulate targeted neurons from anywhere in the world.

articles.title: Former ESC president judged guilty of severe misconduct over drug ties
articles.description: A British cardiologist and former president of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) has been judged by the ESC to have committed severe misconduct after a Danish TV documentary reported that he had been involved in drawing up guidelines for the use of the heart drug ivabradine (Corlanor, Procoralan) while profiting from lucrative contracts with the drug's maker.

articles.title: Customers are trading down in tough consumer environment: Wesfarmers CFO
articles.description: Anthony Gianotti, Group CFO of Australian conglomerate Wesfarmers, discusses the firm's full-year results and the shifting retail environment due to the challenging economic conditions. He also adds that the company's lithium refining operations are expected to reach nameplate capacity by the end of FY2027.

articles.title: Amid the 'Lag 7', Nvidia results make it hard to argue AI cycle is running out of room: CIO
articles.description: Prime Capital Financial CIO Will McGoff discusses Nvidia’s latest earnings report, what it signals about the AI investment cycle, and why he sees a potential catch-up trade in the Magnificent Seven stocks. He also touches on Nvidia's potential in China.

articles.title: Smart nanoparticles light up brain cancer and destroy what surgery misses
articles.description: Scientists created smart nanoparticles that can both illuminate hidden glioblastoma cells during surgery and destroy microscopic cancer left behind afterward. In mice, the treatment prevented recurrence and led to 100% survival at 60 days, though it has not yet been tested in humans.

articles.title: Pancreatic cancer drug approval: FDA OKs Revolution Medicines' daily pills
articles.description: U.S. health officials have approved a groundbreaking pancreatic cancer drug that offers a new approach to treating the deadly form of cancer. The Food and Drug Administration granted approval Wednesday to the first-of-a-kind pill from Revolution Medicines. The drug uses a new approach to block a protein that fuels tumor growth in the vast majority of pancreatic cancer cases. Patients taking the drug nearly doubled their survival time in a company study. Experts say the treatment will likely revamp their approach to the disease and other hard-to-treat cancers. Other companies are researching drugs with similar actions.

articles.title: Tim Archer, Lam Research CEO: A Fortt Knox Update
articles.description: Lam Research CEO Tim Archer told Jon Fortt the chip equipment maker will spend $3 billion over several years to expand its global R&D lab network — breaking ground in Oregon plus other U.S., Asian and European sites — to meet AI-driven demand, especially high-bandwidth memory. Archer argued AI is disrupting memory's classic boom-bust cycle since every logic, memory and storage chip now shapes AI performance, played down overbuild fears, and said Lam is hiring "everywhere."
